Bay layout changes over time must not corrupt history — record the map version alongside events. History must survive a service restart; a restart test is the acceptance gate.

title: Frontend reports bayState transitions over WS
description: New WS message (e.g. bayState, sent on confirmed transitions only, batched) so the frontend — the one place with the bay map — reports state changes and dwell starts to the server. Occupancy math stays frontend-only (invariant 5); do not duplicate it in Python. Update protocol types in src/net/protocol.ts and server schemas in the same change.

title: Honest 'cannot confirm' bay state
description: Extend the bay state model with an explicit unconfirmed value (shown gray) used when detections are stale (older than a configurable window), inference is degraded/offline, or matching confidence is below the trust threshold. The board must never silently freeze on last-known state — 'we don't know' is a first-class display state (VISION rule: Trustworthy).

title: Per-bay 'since when' duration on the board
description: Show how long each bay has been in its current state. Duration is recomputed from the store snapshot's state-transition timestamp on each store emit (no per-component timers). Exported pure duration-formatting helper (e.g. '6 min', '1 h 12 m') with unit tests. Displayed on bay cards and the new board tile.

title: Stabilized bay-state layer: debounce + hysteresis
description: Add a pure, unit-testable module between raw per-frame occupancy results and the store that publishes a bay state change only after it has held for a configurable duration (time-based debounce in seconds, not frames) and applies different thresholds/hold times for entering vs leaving a state (hysteresis). Kills visible flicker from near-miss maneuvers and momentary detection dropouts. Store snapshot gains per-bay state-transition timestamps. Vitest coverage in a pure module, no three.js/WS glue.

title: A yard with memory: occupancy history, dwell times, and alerts
description: VISION.md stage 2. Once the live board is trusted, the product stops being a window and becomes a record. A yard controller should never lose the yard's history when a shift ends, and an operations lead should never have to settle a 'how long was that truck sitting there?' argument from memory. This epic adds: per-bay occupancy timelines (what happened, when), dwell tracking (how long each truck has been parked, per bay and per carrier where identifiable), and a small set of high-value alerts surfaced to the right person without anyone watching — blocked bay, truck dwelling past its window, yard activity overnight. Customer value: yesterday's shift is a timeline, not a guess; problems are surfaced before someone stumbles into them; disputes get settled with facts. Serves the VISION.md rule that the yard's state has a memory. Technical breakdown TBD — outcome first: the record must survive restarts, be shareable (a shift supervisor can pull it up), and require zero extra effort from the controller.
design:
TECHNICAL STEPS (directional — child issues to be scoped from these)

1. Get bay states to the backend (single source of truth)
   - Occupancy is derived in the frontend today. Introduce a new WS message (e.g. `bayState`, batched per confirmed transition, echoing frameId semantics) so the frontend — the one place that has the bay map — reports state changes and dwell starts to the server. Do not duplicate occupancy math in Python.

2. Durable record
   - New server-side persistence (SQLite to start; schema: bay id, state, since, until, source frame/time, confidence) written from a new recorder module in the server app. History must survive service restarts — a restart test is an acceptance gate.
   - Bay layout changes over time must not corrupt history: record the bay map version alongside events.

3. History API
   - New REST surface under `/api/history`: per-bay timeline over a time range, per-bay dwell summaries, shift/day rollups. Read-only; pydantic schemas; no pixels ever stored.

4. Timeline & dwell UI
   - New history view (separate route): horizontal per-bay timeline for a chosen shift/day, plus dwell column added to the live board (ties into the "since when" work in the trusted-board epic).
   - Shift picker defaults to "last night" / "current shift" — zero-effort for the controller.

5. Alerts
   - New alert rules evaluated on confirmed state events, with rules as data (dwell window per bay belongs in `bays.json`-style config, not code): bay occupied past its dwell window; bay occupied by a truck that never leaves (blocked/overstay); overnight/after-hours activity.
   - Alerts persist with the record and surface in a new UI notification surface; "right person" starts as in-app + a webhook out (email/SMS integration deferred, pluggable).

6. Multi-viewer & late joiners
   - On WS connect, the server replies with current bay states + dwell so a second viewer (supervisor pulling up the board) sees the same truth immediately; history comes from the API, not the live socket.

7. Tests
   - Recorder, alert rules, and dwell computation as pure logic with an injectable clock; API tests with a stubbed event feed; restart-persistence test.
acceptance_criteria: From the users' point of view: (1) a bay's occupancy over any past shift can be reviewed as a timeline, (2) dwell time per occupied bay is visible live and historically, (3) a blocked-bay or overstay condition reaches the right person without anyone watching the board, (4) history survives a service restart and is available to more than one viewer.

title: Trusted live occupancy: a bay board a controller can act on
description: VISION.md stage 1, hardened. Today the product shows bay states; a yard controller still can't fully trust them for the 'which bay can I send this truck to?' decision. This epic makes the live board decision-grade: bay states that stay stable through flicker and near-miss maneuvers (state changes must reflect reality, not frame noise), a per-bay 'since when' (how long occupied/free), an honest 'can't confirm' state instead of a guess, and glanceable presentation a controller can read from across the room in under 5 seconds. Customer value: the radio call 'is bay 3 free?' gets answered by a glance, and the answer is believed. Product rules from VISION.md this epic serves: Glanceable, Trustworthy. Technical breakdown into child issues is TBD — this epic sets the outcome, not the implementation.
design:
TECHNICAL STEPS (directional — child issues to be scoped from these)

1. Stabilized bay-state layer (kills flicker)
   - Add a new pure, unit-testable module in the frontend occupancy pipeline that sits between raw per-frame occupancy results and the store: a bay state change publishes only after it has held for a configurable duration (time-based debounce in seconds, not frames — capture rate varies).
   - Add hysteresis: use different thresholds/hold times for entering vs leaving a state, so near-miss maneuvers and momentary detection dropouts don't flip states.
   - The store snapshot gains a per-bay "state since" timestamp set only on confirmed transitions.

2. "Since when" on every bay
   - New UI element on each bay card / board tile rendering the duration in its current state, recomputed from the snapshot timestamp on each store emit (no per-component timers).
   - Duration formatting helper as an exported pure function (e.g. "6 min", "1 h 12 m") with unit tests.

3. Honest "cannot confirm" state
   - Extend the bay state model with an explicit `unconfirmed` value, shown gray, used when: detections are stale (older than a configurable window), inference is degraded/offline, or detection confidence/matching is below the trust threshold.
   - The board must never silently freeze on a last-known state — "we don't know" is a first-class display state (VISION rule: Trustworthy).

4. Glanceable board view
   - New full-viewport board component (one large color block per bay: state + duration, minimal text) readable from across a room, responsive down to tablet; the existing sidebar cards remain the detail view.
   - Verify the <5-second read on desktop and tablet; test with a resized window.

5. Tests & invariants
   - Debounce/hysteresis/duration logic lives in pure modules with Vitest coverage (no three.js or WS glue).
   - State still flows one way through the immutable store; the overlay canvas continues to draw only boxes/rects — no status text moves onto canvas.
acceptance_criteria: From the controller's point of view: (1) bay states do not visibly flicker during normal yard activity, (2) each bay shows how long it has been in its current state, (3) the UI distinguishes 'empty', 'occupied', and 'cannot confirm' honestly, (4) the state of the whole yard is readable in under 5 seconds on desktop and tablet.

comments.author: Jake Helfrich
comments.text: BLOCKER (domain gap, not pipeline): letterbox 16:9 alignment fix shipped and verified (commit 664d090); live e2e in YOLO mode shows real latencyMs/inferenceMs on HUD (infer 30ms, latency 31ms @ 10fps capture), boxes/bays aligned at non-16:9 window. But stock COCO yolov8n detects ZERO trucks on real sim frames — offline experiment across 3 captured frames x {native, 2x Lanczos upscale} x imgsz {640, 960, 1280}: no truck/car/bus above noise; yolov8s: none; yolov8m: sporadic truck conf 0.11-0.32 (below 0.35 threshold) at 220-360ms/frame. Bead acceptance 'real trucks detected from the sim' needs a fine-tuned model — exactly bead cfr.2 (synthetic-data fine-tuning loop). Note: yolov8m via PARKING_MODEL_NAME is viable after fine-tuning; PARKING_IMGSZ knob + README benchmark (320->12ms, 640->34ms, 960->80ms, 1280->128ms on yolov8n) landed with cfr. Leaving open per ralph rules; recommend closing 0ak.2 after cfr.2 lands and re-running this verification.

comments.author: Jake Helfrich
comments.text:
TRAINING RUN LOG (fine-tuned model that resolves the domain-gap blocker; reproducible recipe committed in server/scripts/):

DIAGNOSIS FIRST (offline, before any training): stock COCO yolov8n = 0 trucks on 3 real sim captures x {native, 2x Lanczos} x imgsz {640,1280} (only noise classes: chair/airplane/clock). yolov8s: zero. yolov8m: sporadic truck conf 0.11-0.32, 220-360ms/frame. => domain gap: COCO trucks are textured photos, sim trucks are flat-shaded low-poly boxes. Decision: adapt the model to the sim (cheap, certain), not the sim to COCO (expensive, speculative).

DATASET (zero human labeling):
1. Added frontend ?gt=1 debug mode (frontend/src/scene/gt.ts): renders the sim normally, captures clean 960x540 JPEGs at ~2fps via FrameCapture(500ms interval), projects EXACT truck bboxes from the three.js scene graph (THREE.Box3.setFromObject per truck group, 8 corners through camera.project() -> NDC -> normalized top-left: x=(ndc.x+1)/2, y=(1-ndc.y)/2; skips boxes with corners behind camera). POSTs {id, jpeg:base64, width, height, boxes} to a local collector. Not part of the demo pipeline/wire protocol.
2. server/scripts/gt_collect.py: tiny HTTP collector (:9999/frame) appending records to JSONL. Collected ~4 min => 511 frames, 2293 boxes, 0-6 trucks/frame, all lifecycle phases.
3. server/scripts/make_yolo_dataset.py: JSONL -> Ultralytics dataset (images/labels x train/val 90/10, class 0=truck, boxes <6px dropped as unlearnable, seed 42). YOLO labels share our normalized top-left origin; conversion is corner->center only, no flip. => 453 train / 50 val.

TRAINING (server/scripts/train_simtruck.py): yolov8n.pt transfer-learned on simtruck.yaml, imgsz 960 (=native capture res, keeps small trucks), 50 epochs, batch 8, device=mps (Apple Silicon GPU), ~35s/epoch, ~30min total. Results.csv (val): epoch 2 P=0.98 R=0.97 mAP50=0.993; epoch 4 P=0.999 R=0.991 mAP50=0.995; plateaued. Held-out sim frames previously blind to stock yolov8n now get 5-7 trucks at conf up to 0.99.

SERVER CHANGE: app/detection.py now resolves allowed_classes against the LOADED model's own names mapping (fine-tuned truck=0, COCO truck=7) instead of the hardcoded COCO table. Deploy: PARKING_DETECTOR=yolo PARKING_MODEL_NAME=simtruck.pt (weights gitignored; copy locally).

Artifacts (ephemeral /tmp, regenerate via the scripts): /tmp/simtruck-gt/{raw.jsonl, dataset/, runs/simtruck/, train.log}

- MAX_ACTIVE drops from 8 to match 4 bays (mockup caps active actors at 3 so the lane never gridlocks).
- Spawn direction alternation still keys off bay index; confirm the truck clears the bay mouth before the yaw tween starts now that it is 7.2 m long.
- Determinism is a hard requirement: no Math.random.
acceptance_criteria: Trucks come to rest square inside the paint with no overhang past the back line, and the lane never deadlocks with all bays full.

title: Depot yard scene overhaul: 4 far-side bays, rigid truck model, depot scenery
description:
Rebuild the three.js sim scene so the demo reads as a real logistics yard instead of an abstract test lot. Approved from the live mockup at https://claude.ai/code/artifact/34d7b302-bcb4-49ca-8d11-c97cb5e78259 (options: 'Far side · 4 bays' + 'Rigid' + 'Depot').

Three user-visible changes:
1. Bays: 8 (4 north + 4 south) becomes 4, far/north side only. The near rank sat between the camera and the lane, stacking its overlay boxes over the far ones.
2. Vehicle: replace the 5-box truck with a 7.2 m rigid box truck (day cab, roof deflector, ribbed body, chassis rails, bumper, mirrors, mudflaps, marker lamps, hubbed wheels).
3. Scenery: warehouse dock wall behind the bays, kerbs, painted bay numbers, mast lights, fence, hedge, treeline, distant hills, gradient sky dome and retuned fog.
4. Camera: reframe head-on to the dock wall, approved by the user from the mockup screenshot.

Scope is frontend/src/scene/* plus frontend/public/bays.json. No protocol, server, or occupancy-logic change: invariants 1-6 in AGENTS.md all hold (bays stay data, the model still only detects trucks, render stays decoupled from inference).
design:
Target geometry, taken from the approved mockup (fov 55, 16:9):
- BAY_COUNT = 4, north side only. BAY_WIDTH 3.4, BAY_GAP 1.2, BAY_DEPTH 8.4 (rigid truck 7.2 m + clearance), LANE_WIDTH 8.
- Bay centre z = -(LANE_WIDTH/2 + BAY_DEPTH/2) = -8.2; bays span 18.4 m along X.
- Camera: orbit theta 0.02, phi 0.40, radius 45 about target (0, 2.2, -7) => camera.position ~ (0.9, 19.6, 34.9), lookAt(0, 2.2, -7). Keep fov 55 and the fixed 16:9 projection.
- bays.json must be regenerated from THIS camera; the mockup is the reference for what the four rects should look like.
acceptance_criteria:
- Sidebar reads '4 monitored'; all four bays are north.
- A rigid truck parks inside its bay paint with no overhang, and the bay flips to OCCUPIED.
- npm run build passes; existing vitest suites pass unchanged.
- Manual e2e smoke with the server running: boxes render, bay states flip.
notes:
REFERENCE: design/scene/depot-mockup.html — working three.js source for the approved scene (open it in a browser; see design/scene/README.md for query params and dimensions). Port the geometry and the numbers, not the style: the mockup is untyped ES5-ish JS, the codebase is strict TS. Live copy: https://claude.ai/code/artifact/34d7b302-bcb4-49ca-8d11-c97cb5e78259

Camera framing is still being tuned; confirm the default view against the mockup before deriving bays.json from it.
close_reason: Depot yard overhaul shipped: 4 far-side bays, rigid box truck, warehouse/treeline scenery, reframed camera — documented in README; simtruck weights retrained on the finished scene (mAP50 0.995, live e2e verified). Closed at user direction.

title: Operations insight: from a visible yard to a measurable, improvable one
description: VISION.md stage 4. With live occupancy trusted and a history recorded, the yard stops being merely visible and becomes measurable — and improvable. This epic turns accumulated occupancy and dwell data into decisions: which bays turn around fastest, where trucks idle longest, which carriers dwell past their windows, where a fifth bay would pay for itself. Customer value: the operations lead gets the weekly-review artifact that used to take a spreadsheet project, and the case for physical yard changes writes itself from data. Serves the VISION.md through-line — we sell minutes back to people; this stage is where the sold minutes become visible to the buyer. Technical breakdown TBD. Deliberately out of scope per VISION.md: replacing the site's yard-management system (we make it better informed), and anything approaching driver identification or surveillance — insight is about bays and flows, not people.
design:
TECHNICAL STEPS (directional — child issues to be scoped from these)

1. Aggregation layer (backend)
   - New read-only reporting endpoints built purely on the history store: per-bay turnaround times (empty→occupied→empty cycle durations), dwell distributions, utilization percentage, busiest/idle-est hours. No new inference, no pixels — SQL/aggregation over recorded events only.

2. Insight UI
   - New "review" route: weekly/shift view with a small set of glanceable charts — turnaround by bay, dwell over time, utilization heatmap, bottleneck ranking. Charts must obey the glanceable rule (readable in seconds, not dashboards-for-analysts).

3. Export & share
   - CSV export endpoints for the raw aggregates, plus a printable/shareable weekly-report page (print stylesheet rather than PDF generation to start) so the ops lead can bring it to the weekly review.

4. Carrier dimension — optional and opt-in
   - Where a site wants per-carrier comparison, carriers enter as a manual label (gate check-in) or an integration hook to the site's yard-management system; the model never identifies anything from pixels (VISION: we watch bays, not people). All insight views must be fully useful without carrier data.

5. No surveillance creep
   - Guardrail in both data model and UI: aggregates are about bays, flows, and durations. No per-vehicle identity, no plate capture, no person detection.

6. Tests
   - Aggregation correctness covered against synthetic history fixtures (known cycles → known turnarounds/dwell), including gap handling for restarts and bay-map changes.
acceptance_criteria: From the operations lead's point of view: (1) bay turnaround and dwell patterns are reviewable per shift/week without manual data work, (2) bottleneck bays and over-dwelling patterns are identifiable at a glance, (3) an export or shareable report exists for the weekly ops review, (4) no insight requires identifying individuals.
